Citigroup drops 4% and Bank of America falls 3%, with trader positioning rather than company-specific news driving Citigroup's steeper decline.

XLF falls roughly 1% while SPY slips just 0.3%, confirming selling pressure is concentrated in large bank stocks, not the broad market.

Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $39 million to settle claims it swept idle retirement cash into accounts paying near-zero interest.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Selling across financial stocks is landing hardest on some of the biggest U.S. banks, and Citigroup (NYSE:C) shares are leading the money-center names lower as traders pull back from the group. Citigroup stock is down 4% to $123.81, posting the largest decline among the large banks.

_ultraforma_ / Getty Images

Meanwhile, Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) stock is down 3% to $53.07, a smaller drop than Citigroup stock is posting despite a fresh legal headline from the Merrill Lynch unit. JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) stock is down 0.9% to $327.81, the smallest pullback of the three and a sign that sellers are drawing clear lines between the biggest banks.

Meanwhile, the Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (NYSEARCA:XLF) is down 0.99% to $52.87, a smaller decline than Citigroup and Bank of America shares are showing. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.3% to $760.54, so equities overall are seeing only a modest pullback.

Merrill Lynch Settlement Lands at Bank of America

Bank of America's Merrill Lynch unit will pay $39 million to settle a class action over cash sweep accounts, Reuters reported. Settlement papers were filed late Wednesday in Manhattan federal court, and the case centered on idle retirement cash that customers stated Merrill Lynch swept into deposit accounts paying very little interest. Approval from U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni is still required, and the agreement avoids a trial that had been set for mid-October.

title: 214-year-old Wall Street bank just reversed its biggest call of the summer
detail:
214-year-old Wall Street bank just reversed its biggest call of the summer
Anand Sinha
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 11:41 AM CDT 2 min read
ETH-USD
BTC-USD
C
Trade ETH on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

One of Wall Street's oldest institutions spent the summer telling clients that the market's most divisive asset was headed lower.

That asset responded with the best third quarter it has ever had. On Wednesday, the bank changed its mind.

Citigroup raised its 12-month price targets for Bitcoin and Ethereum, which is the world's second-largest cryptocurrency by more than 35%, Reuters reported on Oct. 1.

The bank now sees Bitcoin at $113,000 and Ether at $3,028 within a year, up from the $82,000 and $2,240 it forecast when it slashed both targets three months ago.

A price target is a bank's best estimate of where an asset will trade over a set horizon, and the research behind it shapes how its wealth managers and institutional clients position. Which is what makes the timing of this one notable.

For context, Citi traces its lineage to the City Bank of New York, chartered in 1812, the year the United States went to war with Britain. The institution has outlasted the Civil War, the Great Depression and the 2008 crisis it barely survived.

Related: Legendary trader who nailed Bitcoin's 2018 crash makes bold new call

When Citi slashed Bitcoin, Ether targets in July

Citi cut its targets on July 1, citing weak investor appetite, outflows from crypto exchange-traded funds and stalled legislation in Washington. Its bear case saw Bitcoin as low as $53,000 and Ether at $1,094.

July 1 also happened to be the first day of what became Bitcoin's best third quarter on record, a 42.7% return against a historical Q3 average of 8.7%, according to CoinGlass. Ether did better still, returning roughly 54% over the three months. Both assets have now clawed their way back to within 5% and 10% of where they started 2026.

The round trip took 92 days. Citi's new $113,000 Bitcoin target sits a thousand dollars above where its target stood before the July cut. Ether never got its old number back; the new $3,028 target remains below the $3,175 the bank projected before summer.

What the bank says changed

The bank cites stronger crypto activity, a supportive economic backdrop, and the return of ETF inflows, the same money whose exit spooked it in June. It now expects about $5 billion of inflows over the next 12 months, slower but steadier than the earlier boom, as financial advisers and brokerages gradually add Bitcoin to client portfolios.

Bank of America raised its quarterly dividend to $0.32, but its 11.2% CET1 ratio sits just 1.2 points above the 10% regulatory floor.

JPMorgan's 14.3% and Citigroup's 13.2% CET1 ratios give peers far more capital to return while BAC's 8% loan growth consumes its buffer.

BAC spent $6B on buybacks versus $2B on dividends in Q2, treating repurchases as the flexible valve that protects the sticky dividend commitment.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

Bank of America (NYSE:BAC) raised its quarterly common dividend to $0.32 from $0.28, declared on July 24, 2026. The annualized forward payout now stands at $1.28 per share. Second-quarter EPS was $1.21, and the bank paid $2.0B in common dividends against $9.07B of net income. Capital is the constraint.

majaiva / iStock Unreleased via Getty Images
BAC Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Why Record Profits Still Hit a Capital Ceiling

As a systemically important bank, Bank of America must hold common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital above a regulatory floor. Every dollar paid out reduces that pool. Every new loan raises risk-weighted assets, which raises required capital. CFO Alastair Borthwick laid out the math during July's earnings call:

"Tier 1 common equity grew to nearly $202 billion while our RWA increased to $1.8 trillion driven by loan growth and capital markets activity."

"We remain in a strong position with our CET1 ratio stable at 11.2% and that remains well ahead of our 10% minimum ratio."

That reserve is the smallest among peers. JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) reported a 14.3% CET1 ratio in Q1 2026, and Citigroup (NYSE:C) ended 2025 at 13.2%. Bank of America's average loans rose 8% to $1.2 trillion, consuming capital peers with more slack can return.

Stress Tests Set the Payout Calendar

The Fed's annual stress test resets each bank's buffer, and dividend increases arrive after summer results. CEO Brian Moynihan tied credit discipline to those results on the July 14, 2026 call:

Citigroup Lifts Bitcoin Target to $113K, Ether to $3,028

Citigroup (NYSE: $C) raised its 12-month price forecasts for Bitcoin (CRYPTO: $BTC) and Ethereum (CRYPTO: $ETH) on Wednesday, pointing to stronger crypto market activity, a more supportive macroeconomic backdrop and a resumption of ETF inflows.

The bank lifted its bitcoin target to $113,000 from $82,000 and its ether target to $3,028 from $2,240, according to a client note. Citi also forecast $5 billion in crypto inflows over the next 12 months, expecting the pace to stay slower and steadier as financial advisers and brokerages gradually raise their bitcoin allocations rather than moving in a single rush.

The revision follows a sharp run for both assets. Bitcoin has climbed nearly 40% and ether about 68% over the past three months, narrowing their year-to-date losses to roughly 4% and 9%, respectively. Citi tied bitcoin's rebound from its July lows partly to a weaker dollar, which gained support after the U.S. Treasury's recent move to buy back longer-dated bonds.

A record Electron launch contract and a new Wall Street initiation reached Rocket Lab (NASDAQ:RKLB) within hours of each other. It gained a signed deal and fresh bull case. Rocket Lab stock is up 5% to $72.88 in morning trading, leading a space group posting far smaller gains.

Notably, the Procure Space ETF (NASDAQ:UFO) is up 0.3% to $42.46, a muted gain for a fund built around launch providers, satellite operators and aerospace contractors. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $764.90, a modest advance for U.S. equities that leaves the move in Rocket Lab stock looking clearly company-driven.

Also, AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock is up 2% to $59.80, a smaller gain that trails the advance in Rocket Lab stock. Trading close to flat, SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) stock is up 0.1% to $151.07, even though the contract news landed on a direct launch rival. That muted response from both keeps the spotlight squarely on Rocket Lab.

Record Electron Contract Lifts Backlog Past 100 Missions

Rocket Lab announced a multi-year launch agreement for 20 new Electron missions with Synspective, a Tokyo-based Earth observation company, in a release issued after the previous close. The deal is the biggest commercial launch contract for Electron in Rocket Lab's history, making Synspective the company's largest Electron customer, and Synspective's radar imaging satellites will fly from Rocket Lab's own launch complex, with the missions scheduled annually later this decade.
